summary: Verified bug fix: clicking 'Start the timed test' (aptitude-start-btn) on the JPM aptitude intro NO LONGER crashes with the 'A glitch in the cosmos' React error boundary. Flow tested end-to-end as mocktest@valuevade.test → /interview-sims → Resume JPM → filled application (4 textareas, 30+ chars each) → submitted → Application Shortlisted screen → Continue to Online Aptitude Test → aptitude-intro → clicked aptitude-start-btn. Button correctly flipped to 'Preparing your test…' spinner and remained in that state during 5 polling POSTs to /api/interview-sim/attempt/{id}/aptitude/start (all 200 OK). Test view rendered at ~18s with all 12 questions, 48 option buttons (12x4), timer counting down from 14:59, and Submit test button present. Clicked Q1 option A and progress correctly updated 0/12 → 1/12. NO React error boundary, NO whole-page crash, NO toast error observed.
critical_code_review_comments: AptitudeStage.jsx guards are correctly in place: test-view branch is gated by `test && Array.isArray(test.questions) && test.questions.length > 0`; per-question options use `Array.isArray(q?.options) ? q.options : []`; ReviewAccordion is guarded by `Array.isArray(review)` and per-row `Array.isArray(r?.options)` with null-safe correct/given lookups. The prior crash on `.length` of undefined is no longer reachable.
Polling loop (lines 42-57) is clean: max ~120s cap, catches transient failures with warn+retry, and throws user-visible errors that surface as toast (never as an uncaught render error).
Auto-submit useEffect (line 90-93) correctly guards on submittedRef to prevent double submissions.
